submissions.note: ONE PLAN FOR THE WHOLE CONTRACT — thirteen pieces, wave 3 to wave 19, and then I intend to say nothing but HOLD. Three attempts taught this shape. A rider that re-commands mid-run pays twice: once because a submission REPLACES the record set and throws away the reflex layer's staging, and once because every trigger it outlived while thinking fires on the same tick, where all but one must fail against a single parked mouse. The cure is not to answer faster, it is to plan far enough ahead that answering is unnecessary. Wave triggers, two apart at the top and one apart later, so no two ever come due together. Bench of four turrets first (50/70/95/125 by wave 9), then six beacons through wave 16 as the pulse thickens, then palisades — 10 gold each, the cheapest hit-points on the board — for the last three waves. 720 gold against a 1.4x pan across 570 seconds. Cells are named as intent across the working middle; the reflex layer relocates each toward whichever seam is paying, and now also refuses to stand and pan inside a 24-strong pulse below three-quarters health, which is exactly how the last attempt died at wave 18 with all four turrets still standing.

HOLD. Turret one down at wave 3 on its cell, purse 171, twelve pieces queued and nothing due for another wave. Same gate plan as the last attempt — the only things that changed are on my side of the fence: the reflex layer now re-opens a collapsed build menu before it trusts a tile click, and it stops working seams once there is nothing left to buy.

HOLD. Read the view, nothing in it argues with the gate plan: the ladder is funded, the works are standing, and the next piece is waiting on its wave rather than on me. Restating would replace the record set and throw away the reflex layer stagings for no gain.

briefing.geography: Mesa country; dry washes fall toward one sunken spring.
goals: Work the dry washes around the lone spring.
rules: Sluices work only beside the spring.
The river is gone; enemies can press from every edge.
